# Realtime Collaborative To-Do List with RedwoodSDK

## Background

You are working in an existing RedwoodSDK (rwsdk) project. RedwoodSDK is a server-first React framework for the Cloudflare platform that ships a built-in realtime primitive, the `useSyncedState` hook, backed by a `SyncedStateServer` Durable Object. Your job is to turn the starter app into a realtime collaborative to-do list: any item added by one connected client must appear, in realtime, on every other client viewing the same page.

## Requirements

* The home route `/` must render an interactive to-do list page.
* The list of to-do items must be shared state synchronized across all connected clients using RedwoodSDK's realtime `useSyncedState` primitive (not local `useState`, not polling). The state is global (all clients on `/` share one list; no per-room scoping).
* A user can type text into an input and add it as a new to-do item. Adding an item on one client must cause that item to appear on all other clients that currently have `/` open, without a manual page reload.
* Existing items must remain visible to a client that connects after items were already added (server is the source of truth).
* The client components must actually hydrate in the browser (event handlers and effects must run).

## Implementation Hints

* Review the RedwoodSDK realtime documentation for `useSyncedState` (`https://docs.rwsdk.com/experimental/realtime`). The hook mirrors React's `useState` but takes an additional unique state key and synchronizes bidirectionally with the server.
* Model the shared list as a single synced value (e.g. an array) under one shared key so every client subscribes to the same state.
* Wire up the realtime backend end-to-end: the `SyncedStateServer` Durable Object must be exported from the worker entry and its routes registered, and the Durable Object must be declared in `wrangler.jsonc` (including the SQLite migration via `new_sqlite_classes`). After changing bindings you may need to regenerate types.
* Because RedwoodSDK is server-first, the interactive component must be a client component and the HTML Document must load the client hydration script, otherwise handlers and realtime updates will not run.
* Keep the interactive parts in a `"use client"` component and import the hook from `rwsdk/use-synced-state/client`.
* The realtime primitive relies on an additional peer package that is not installed by default; if it is missing, the framework surfaces a clear runtime error naming the package to install. Add it to the project's dependencies.

## Runtime & Interface Contract

* Project path: /home/user/project
* Start command: `npm run dev`
* Port: 5173 (the app must be reachable at `http://localhost:5173/`)
* Route: `/` renders the collaborative to-do list.
* DOM contract (stable selectors the solution must expose so the list can be driven programmatically):
  * A text input for the new item text with attribute `data-testid="todo-input"`.
  * A button that adds the current input text as a new item with attribute `data-testid="todo-add"`.
  * Each rendered to-do item must be an element with attribute `data-testid="todo-item"` whose visible text content is the item's text.
* Realtime behavior: two browser clients that both have `/` open must converge on the same set of to-do items after either client adds an item.
